source.text: בֶּן־שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִ֖ים יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְאַחַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of eight years [was] Josiah when he became king, and thirty and one year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem.

en.L: A son of eight years [was] Josiah when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
en.B: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
en.R: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a son of eight years: eight years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chronicles 33:1).

decisions.choice: eight years old: made king as a boy after his father was murdered
decisions.reason: Josiah's father Amon was killed by his own officials after reigning two years, and the people of the land made the young Josiah king in his place (33:21-25). The prophecy of 1 Kings 13:2 had named Josiah of the house of David long before.

decisions.choice: the same opening as 2 Kings 22:1, without the king's mother
decisions.reason: Josiah's reign is also told in 2 Kings 22:1-23:30. This verse repeats 2 Kings 22:1 word for word except that it does not name Josiah's mother, Jedidah daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath. Chronicles leaves out the mother's name for the kings of Judah after Hezekiah (33:1, 21; 36:2).

decisions.choice: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years
decisions.reason: The same wording as 2 Kings 22:1 at each level, since the Hebrew is the same; the accession formula kept throughout these books.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדַרְכֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔יו וְלֹא־סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in [the] ways of David his father, and not he turned aside right and left.

en.L: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and walked in the ways of David his father, and he did not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left.
en.B: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and walked in the ways of his ancestor David. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
en.R: Josiah did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right. He lived as his ancestor David had lived, and he did not wander off the path, either to the right or to the left.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict, with no reservation
decisions.reason: This is the good verdict given to the faithful kings (29:2). No limit is added to it, and the chapter goes on to show Josiah seeking God from his youth (verse 3).

decisions.choice: walked in the ways of David his father: lived as his ancestor David had lived
decisions.reason: To walk in a way is to live by a pattern of conduct. "Father" also means a forefather: David lived more than three hundred years earlier, and the kings of Judah are measured against him (17:3; 29:2).

decisions.choice: did not turn aside to the right or to the left: the words Deuteronomy uses for keeping the law
decisions.reason: God's commands are pictured as a road not to be left in either direction (Deuteronomy 5:32; 28:14). The king is to read the law all his life and "not turn aside from the commandment, right or left" (Deuteronomy 17:18-20). The verse is the same as 2 Kings 22:2, except that Chronicles says "the ways" of David where Kings says "all the way"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right; his ancestor David; did not wander off the path
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:2 at each level, with "the ways" for the plural Hebrew. Readable keeps "wander off the path" so that the echo of Deuteronomy (m3) can be heard.

source.text: וּבִשְׁמוֹנֶ֨ה שָׁנִ֜ים לְמָלְכ֗וֹ וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ נַ֔עַר הֵחֵ֕ל לִדְר֕וֹשׁ לֵאלֹהֵ֖י דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו וּבִשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה הֵחֵל֙ לְטַהֵ֔ר אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִן־הַבָּמוֹת֙ וְהָ֣אֲשֵׁרִ֔ים וְהַפְּסִלִ֖ים וְהַמַּסֵּכֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] eighth year of his reigning, and he still [was] a youth, he began to seek [the] God of David his father; and in [the] twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the Asherah poles and the carved images and the cast images.

en.L: And in the eighth year of his reign, while he [was] still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the Asherah poles and the carved images and the cast images.
en.B: In his eighth year as king, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem, clearing away the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images and the cast images.
en.R: In the eighth year that Josiah was king, when he was still a young man of about sixteen, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. Four years later he began to clear Judah and Jerusalem of the hilltop shrines, the poles used to worship Asherah, and the idols carved from wood or stone or made from melted metal.

decisions.choice: the eighth and the twelfth year: when Josiah was about sixteen and about twenty
decisions.reason: Josiah became king at eight (verse 1). His eighth year as king was when he was about sixteen, and his twelfth when he was about twenty. The word for "youth" is used for a boy or a young man not yet fully grown in standing (1 Kings 3:7).

decisions.choice: seek the God of David: turn to him in worship, trust and obedience
decisions.reason: In Chronicles, to seek God is more than asking for guidance: it is to turn to him with one's whole life (see 1 Chronicles 10:14; 2 Chronicles 14:3). Josiah's father and grandfather had served other gods (33:2-7, 22); the young king turns to the God of David.

decisions.choice: the reform begins before the book is found
decisions.reason: 2 Kings tells the whole reform after the finding of the book in Josiah's eighteenth year (2 Kings 22:3-23:20). Chronicles says that Josiah began to seek God in his eighth year and to purge the land in his twelfth, and tells the finding of the book afterwards (verse 8). Kings gathers all the reform into one account after the finding of the book; Chronicles tells it in stages.

decisions.choice: high places, Asherah poles, carved images, cast images: the places and objects of false worship
decisions.reason: The high places were local places of worship (14:2). The Asherah poles stood for the goddess Asherah. Carved images were shaped from wood or stone, and cast images were made by pouring molten metal into a mold. The law forbade both kinds (Deuteronomy 27:15), and Manasseh had set them up (33:3, 19, 22).

decisions.choice: cleanse: make clean by removing what defiled the land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for making something ritually clean. The objects of false worship had made the land unclean, and removing them made it fit for Yahweh's worship again, as Hezekiah had cleansed the temple (29:15-18).

decisions.choice: high places, Asherah poles, carved images, cast images (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines, poles used to worship Asherah, idols carved ... or made from melted metal (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles. Literal says "cleanse" for the verb, Balanced "purge" and Readable "clear".

decisions.choice: a young man of about sixteen; four years later
decisions.reason: Readable gives Josiah's age and says how much later the twelfth year was, from verse 1 (m1), so that the reader can follow the stages of the reform.

source.text: וַיְנַתְּצ֣וּ לְפָנָ֗יו אֵ֚ת מִזְבְּח֣וֹת הַבְּעָלִ֔ים וְהַֽחַמָּנִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־לְמַ֥עְלָה מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם גִּדֵּ֑עַ וְ֠הָאֲשֵׁרִים וְהַפְּסִלִ֤ים וְהַמַּסֵּכוֹת֙ שִׁבַּ֣ר וְהֵדַ֔ק וַיִּזְרֹק֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַקְּבָרִ֔ים הַזֹּבְחִ֖ים לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they tore down before him the altars of the Baals, and the incense altars which [were] above over them he cut down; and the Asherah poles and the carved images and the cast images he broke and he made [them] dust, and he scattered [it] on [the] face of the graves of those sacrificing to them.

en.L: And they tore down before him the altars of the Baals, and the incense altars that [were] above them he cut down; and the Asherah poles and the carved images and the cast images he broke and crushed to dust, and scattered [it] on the surface of the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
en.B: Under his direction they tore down the altars of the Baals, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He smashed the Asherah poles, the carved images and the cast images, crushed them to dust, and scattered the dust over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
en.R: While Josiah watched, the people tore down the altars where Baal was worshiped, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He smashed the poles used to worship Asherah and all the idols, and crushed them into dust. Then he scattered the dust over the graves of the people who had offered sacrifices to them.

decisions.choice: they tore down before him: in his presence, at his command
decisions.reason: "Before him" means in his sight. The people do the work while the king directs it; then the verbs turn to "he", for the work was done on his orders.

decisions.choice: the Baals; incense altars
decisions.reason: "The Baals" is plural, for the many local forms of the god Baal (Judges 2:11; 2 Chronicles 33:3). The word for "incense altars" is rare and its meaning not certain, as at 14:4; it may name small altars for incense or pillars linked with the sun. They stood on or above the altars of the Baals.

decisions.choice: scattered the dust on the graves of those who sacrificed to them: the idols treated as unclean
decisions.reason: Graves made unclean whatever touched them (Numbers 19:16). Throwing the idols' dust on the graves of their worshipers shamed both the idols and those who had served them. 2 Kings 23:6 says that the dust of the Asherah from the temple was thrown on the graves of the common people.

decisions.choice: Under his direction (Balanced); While Josiah watched (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "before him" (m1). Readable says "the altars where Baal was worshiped" for the plural Baals and "all the idols" for the carved and cast images named in verse 3.

source.text: וְעַצְמוֹת֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים שָׂרַ֖ף עַל־מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֑ם וַיְטַהֵ֥ר אֶת־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְאֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And bones of priests he burned on their altars, and he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: And the bones of priests he burned on their altars, and he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and so he purged Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: He burned the bones of the priests on the altars where they had served. In this way he made Judah and Jerusalem clean again.

decisions.choice: burned the bones of priests on their altars: 1 Kings 13:2 fulfilled
decisions.reason: When Jeroboam stood at his altar in Bethel, a man of God cried out that a son of David's house named Josiah would sacrifice on it the priests of the high places and burn human bones on it (1 Kings 13:2). 2 Kings 23:16 and 20 tell how Josiah did this at Bethel and in the towns of Samaria; Chronicles tells it briefly here.

decisions.choice: burning bones on an altar: making it unclean for ever
decisions.reason: A dead body made unclean whatever it touched (Numbers 19:11-16). Burning human bones on the altars defiled them so that they could never be used again. "Their altars" are the altars where these priests had served.

decisions.choice: he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem: the purging begun in verse 3 completed
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 3 comes back: the work Josiah began in his twelfth year is done.

decisions.choice: cleansed (Literal); purged (Balanced); made ... clean again (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the word it used in verse 3. Readable says "the altars where they had served" for "their altars" (m2).

source.text: וּבְעָרֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֧ה וְאֶפְרַ֛יִם וְשִׁמְע֖וֹן וְעַד־נַפְתָּלִ֑י בְּחַרְבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon and as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,

en.L: And in the cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,
en.B: In the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around,
en.R: He did the same in the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, and as far north as Naphtali, in the ruined places all around them.

decisions.choice: in their ruins: the reading in the margin
alternatives: he searched their houses all around
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text here are hard to read; they look like two words, "on the mountain, their houses", or with a small change "he searched their houses". The margin reads one word, followed here, which most likely means "in their ruins"; the same letters can also be read "with their swords", meaning that the work was done with tools of iron. The towns of the north had lain in ruins since the Assyrians destroyed the kingdom of Israel about a century before (2 Kings 17:5-6). The ancient Greek translation reads "in their places all around". The sense of the phrase is not certain.

decisions.choice: Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon and Naphtali: the old northern tribes
decisions.reason: Manasseh and Ephraim were the heart of the old northern kingdom, and Naphtali its far north (2 Kings 15:29). Simeon's towns lay in the south, within Judah's land (Joshua 19:1-9), but some Simeonites seem to have been counted with the north (15:9). Naming them together shows Josiah's reform reaching the land of all the tribes, as Hezekiah had invited all Israel to the Passover (30:1, 10-11).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 7
decisions.reason: The verse names where Josiah worked; verse 7 says what he did there.

decisions.choice: He did the same in ...; as far north as
decisions.reason: Readable makes the verse a sentence of its own by supplying "He did the same", which verse 7 then spells out, and says "north" so that the reader can follow the places. "Cities" is "towns" at Balanced and Readable, as these books do for the smaller places.

source.text: וַיְנַתֵּ֣ץ אֶת־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֗וֹת וְאֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרִ֤ים וְהַפְּסִלִים֙ כִּתַּ֣ת לְהֵדַ֔ק וְכָל־הַֽחַמָּנִ֥ים גִּדַּ֖ע בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and he tore down the altars and the Asherah poles, and the carved images he crushed to make [them] dust, and all the incense altars he cut down in all [the] land of Israel; and he returned [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: and he tore down the altars and the Asherah poles, and the carved images he crushed to dust, and all the incense altars he cut down in all the land of Israel; and he returned [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: he tore down the altars and the Asherah poles, crushed the carved images to dust, and cut down all the incense altars in every part of the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.
en.R: He tore down the altars and the poles used to worship Asherah, and he crushed the idols into dust. He cut down all the incense altars everywhere in the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the land of Israel: the land of all the tribes
decisions.reason: Here "Israel" means the land the twelve tribes had held, including the old northern kingdom, now under Assyrian rule. Chronicles often speaks of all Israel as one people (30:1, 5-6).

decisions.choice: he returned to Jerusalem: as 2 Kings 23:20 ends Josiah's work in the north
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:20 ends its account of the reform in Samaria with the same words, "and he returned to Jerusalem".

decisions.choice: crushed to dust; and he returned [to] Jerusalem / Then he went back to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 23:15 and 20 where the Hebrew is the same. Readable starts a new sentence here, having made verse 6 its own sentence.

source.text: וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ לְטַהֵ֥ר הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהַבָּ֑יִת שָׁ֠לַח אֶת־שָׁפָ֨ן בֶּן־אֲצַלְיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֣הוּ שַׂר־הָעִ֗יר וְ֠אֵת יוֹאָ֤ח בֶּן־יֽוֹאָחָז֙ הַמַּזְכִּ֔יר לְחַזֵּ֕ק אֶת־בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] year eighteen of his reigning, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah and Maaseiah [the] governor of the city and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair [the] house of Yahweh his God.

en.L: And in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had cleansed the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.B: When he had purged the land and the house, in the eighteenth year of his reign, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor and Joah son of Joahaz, the recorder, to make repairs on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.R: In the eighteenth year that Josiah was king, after he had made the land and the temple clean, he sent three officials to repair the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. They were Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah, who governed the city, and Joah son of Joahaz, who kept the records.

decisions.choice: to cleanse the land and the house: when he had cleansed them
alternatives: in order to cleanse the land and the house
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "to cleanse". It most likely marks the time, after the purging of verses 3-7 was done; it may instead give the purpose of the repairs, as the last step in cleansing the temple.

decisions.choice: Maaseiah and Joah sent with Shaphan
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:3 says that Josiah sent Shaphan the scribe, son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, and gives the king's orders about the money (2 Kings 22:4-7). Chronicles names two more officials, Maaseiah the governor of the city and Joah the recorder, and tells what was done rather than what was ordered (verses 9-11).

decisions.choice: the governor of the city; the recorder: royal officials
decisions.reason: The governor of the city was in charge of Jerusalem (1 Kings 22:26). The recorder kept the royal records and announced the king's business (2 Kings 18:18). Shaphan is called the scribe in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the governor of the city / the city governor / who governed the city; the recorder / who kept the records
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 22:26 and 2 Kings 18:18 for these offices. Readable says "temple" for "house", and names the three men in a sentence of their own.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ׀הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֗וֹל וַֽיִּתְּנוּ֮ אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף֮ הַמּוּבָ֣א בֵית־אֱלֹהִים֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָסְפֽוּ־הַלְוִיִּם֩ שֹׁמְרֵ֨י הַסַּ֜ף מִיַּ֧ד מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה וְאֶפְרַ֗יִם וּמִכֹּל֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִכָּל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרֽוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to Hilkiah the priest the great, and they gave the money brought [into the] house of God, which had gathered the Levites, keepers of the threshold, from [the] hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and from all [the] remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And they came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave the money that had been brought [into the] house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the doors had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the rest of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin, and they returned to Jerusalem.
en.R: They went to Hilkiah the high priest and handed him the money that people had brought to God's temple. The Levites who guarded the entrance had collected it from the people of Manasseh and Ephraim, from everyone else left in Israel, and from all the people of Judah and Benjamin. Then they came back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the money the Levites collected: as in 2 Kings 22:4
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:4 speaks of the money "the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people". Chronicles names these doorkeepers as Levites and says that the gifts came from the north, from Manasseh, Ephraim and the rest of Israel, as well as from Judah and Benjamin: the whole people shared in repairing the house of God, as under Joash (24:5-11).

decisions.choice: the remnant of Israel: those left in the north
decisions.reason: The "remnant" are the Israelites who remained in the land of the northern tribes after the Assyrian conquest (30:6; 2 Kings 17:6).

decisions.choice: and they returned to Jerusalem: the reading in the margin
alternatives: and from the inhabitants of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text read "and the inhabitants of Jerusalem", which would add Jerusalem to the list of those who gave. The margin reads, with the same letters differently arranged, "and they returned to Jerusalem", followed here: the Levites who had gone out to collect the money came back to the city. Either reading is possible.

decisions.choice: Hilkiah the high priest
decisions.reason: Literally "the great priest", the title of the chief priest, as in 2 Kings 22:4.

decisions.choice: the Levites who kept the doors (Balanced); the Levites who guarded the entrance (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the duty that "keepers of the threshold" stands for, as 2 Kings 22:4 does; Literal keeps the picture. Readable says "God's temple" for "the house of God".

source.text: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ עַל־יַד֙ עֹשֵׂ֣ה הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה הַמֻּפְקָדִ֖ים בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ עוֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לִבְדּ֥וֹק וּלְחַזֵּ֖ק הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gave [it] on [the] hand of [the] doer of the work, those appointed in [the] house of Yahweh; and they gave it [to the] doers of the work who [were] working in [the] house of Yahweh, to mend and to repair the house.

en.L: And they gave [it] into the hand of the doers of the work, who were appointed in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they gave it [to] the doers of the work who were working in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to mend and to repair the house.
en.B: They handed it to the men doing the work, who had been put in charge of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they paid it to the workmen in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to mend and repair the house.
en.R: Then they gave it to the men who had been put in charge of the work on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. These men used it to pay the workers who were mending and repairing the temple.

decisions.choice: the money handed to the overseers and the workmen: 2 Kings 22:5 carried out
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:5 gives the king's orders in nearly these words: let them give it to the men appointed over the work, and let them give it to the workmen to repair the house. Chronicles tells it as done. It says "to mend and to repair" where Kings says "to repair the breach of the house".

decisions.choice: they gave it to the workmen: the overseers paid the workers
alternatives: and the workmen in the house of Yahweh spent it to mend and repair the house
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 22:5, "the doers of the work" names first the overseers and then the workmen they paid. The second time the Hebrew has no "to", and the words can also be read "and the workmen who were working in the house gave it", that is, spent it on the repairs. The meaning is the same: the money went to the work.

decisions.choice: the doers of the work, who were appointed in the house of the LORD / the men doing the work, who had been put in charge of the house of the LORD
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:5 where the Hebrew is the same. Literal brackets the "to" that the second clause lacks (m2).

source.text: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ לֶחָֽרָשִׁים֙ וְלַבֹּנִ֔ים לִקְנוֹת֙ אַבְנֵ֣י מַחְצֵ֔ב וְעֵצִ֖ים לַֽמְחַבְּר֑וֹת וּלְקָרוֹת֙ אֶת־הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁחִ֖יתוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gave [it] to the craftsmen and to the builders, to buy stones of hewing and timbers for the couplings, and to make beams for the houses which had ruined [the] kings of Judah.

en.L: And they gave [it] to the craftsmen and to the builders, to buy hewn stones and timber for the couplings, and to make beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.
en.B: They gave it to the craftsmen and the builders to buy dressed stone, and timber for the braces and for the beams of the buildings that the kings of Judah had allowed to fall into ruin.
en.R: They gave it to the craftsmen and the builders to buy cut stone and wood. The wood was for joining the walls and for the beams of the buildings that the kings of Judah had let fall apart.

decisions.choice: craftsmen, builders, hewn stone and timber: as in 2 Kings 22:6
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:6 names the same workmen and materials, with the masons as well. Chronicles adds what the timber was for, and that the buildings had been ruined by the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: couplings and beams: timber to bind and roof the buildings
decisions.reason: The first word comes from a verb meaning to join; it names timbers that tied the walls together (1 Chronicles 22:3 uses it of iron clamps). The verb that follows means to lay beams, to put roofs and floors on the buildings.

decisions.choice: the buildings the kings of Judah had ruined: let fall into ruin
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or destroy. The kings before Josiah, Manasseh and Amon above all, had neglected the temple and its buildings and used them for other gods (33:4-7, 22). "The buildings" are the rooms and halls of the temple courts.

decisions.choice: hewn stones / dressed stone / cut stone; couplings / braces / for joining the walls
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:6 for the stone. Literal says "let go to ruin" and Balanced "allowed to fall into ruin" for what the kings did, to show that the ruin came through neglect as well as harm (m3).

source.text: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֩ עֹשִׂ֨ים בֶּאֱמוּנָ֜ה בַּמְּלָאכָ֗ה וַעֲלֵיהֶ֣ם׀מֻ֠פְקָדִים יַ֣חַת וְעֹבַדְיָ֤הוּ הַלְוִיִּם֙ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י וּזְכַרְיָ֧ה וּמְשֻׁלָּ֛ם מִן־בְּנֵ֥י הַקְּהָתִ֖ים לְנַצֵּ֑חַ וְהַ֨לְוִיִּ֔ם כָּל־מֵבִ֖ין בִּכְלֵי־שִֽׁיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the men [were] working in faithfulness in the work; and over them [were] appointed Jahath and Obadiah the Levites from [the] sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from [the] sons of the Kohathites, to oversee; and the Levites, every one skilled in instruments of song,

en.L: And the men were doing the work in faithfulness; and over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to oversee; and the Levites, everyone skilled with instruments of song,
en.B: The men did the work honestly. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the descendants of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the descendants of Kohath, to direct the work. And the Levites, all who were skilled with musical instruments,
en.R: The men worked honestly. The leaders over them were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the family of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the family of Kohath. These men directed the work. Other Levites, all of them skilled musicians,

decisions.choice: doing the work in faithfulness: as 2 Kings 22:7 says of the overseers
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:7 says that no account was asked of those who handled the money, "for they act in faithfulness". Chronicles says the same of the men at work, using the same noun: they could be trusted.

decisions.choice: Levites of Merari and of Kohath: two of the three Levite clans
decisions.reason: The Levites were divided into the clans of Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the sons of Levi (1 Chronicles 6:1; 23:6). Chronicles names Levites from each clan when the temple is cleansed (29:12) and here sets two clans over the work.

decisions.choice: to oversee: to direct the work
decisions.reason: The verb means to lead or direct, and is used of the Levites who directed the building of the temple (1 Chronicles 23:4; Ezra 3:8-9). It is from the same root as the word in many psalm titles for the leader of the music.

decisions.choice: the Levites skilled in music: the sentence goes on into verse 13
alternatives: and the Levites, all skilled in music, accompanied the work
decisions.reason: The words "and the Levites, everyone skilled with instruments of song" begin a new clause that verse 13 finishes: these Levites were over the porters and directed the workmen. Musicians were set over the labor, as the Levites had led worship with music when the temple was cleansed (29:25-30). The words may instead mean that these Levites played music while the work went on, but the Hebrew does not say so.

decisions.choice: did the work honestly (Balanced); worked honestly (Readable); to direct the work
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:7 for "in faithfulness" at Balanced and Readable ("they deal honestly", "they are honest"). "Sons of" a clan's founder is "descendants" at Balanced and "family" at Readable.

source.text: וְעַ֣ל הַסַּבָּלִ֗ים וּֽמְנַצְּחִים֙ לְכֹל֙ עֹשֵׂ֣ה מְלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבוֹדָ֖ה וַעֲבוֹדָ֑ה וּמֵֽהַלְוִיִּ֔ם סוֹפְרִ֥ים וְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וְשׁוֹעֲרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and over the burden-bearers, and [were] overseeing all [the] doer[s] of work for service and service; and from the Levites [were] scribes and officials and gatekeepers.

en.L: and over the burden-bearers, and overseeing all who did the work, for service after service; and of the Levites [some were] scribes and officials and gatekeepers.
en.B: were over the porters and directed all the workmen in every kind of task. Some of the Levites were scribes, officials and gatekeepers.
en.R: were in charge of the men who carried the loads, and they directed all the workers in every kind of job. Some of the Levites were also scribes, officials and gatekeepers.

decisions.choice: over the porters: the musicians of verse 12 in charge of the laborers
decisions.reason: The verse finishes the clause begun at the end of verse 12: the Levites skilled with instruments were over the burden-bearers and directed the workmen. The burden-bearers carried stone and timber (2:1, 17).

decisions.choice: for service and service: for every kind of task
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun with "and" means one after another, every one of its kind.

decisions.choice: scribes, officials and gatekeepers: other Levite duties
decisions.reason: David had appointed Levites as officials and judges, and as gatekeepers of the temple (1 Chronicles 23:4-5; 26:1-19). Scribes kept records and wrote documents (1 Chronicles 24:6). Chronicles shows the Levites serving in all these roles during the repairs.

decisions.choice: porters (Balanced); the men who carried the loads (Readable); officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the work the burden-bearers did. The word for "officials" is rendered as in Deuteronomy 16:18 at every level. Literal brackets "some were", which the Hebrew implies with "of the Levites".

source.text: וּבְהוֹצִיאָ֣ם אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף הַמּוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מָצָא֙ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶת־סֵ֥פֶר תּֽוֹרַת־יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when they brought out the money brought [into the] house of Yahweh, found Hilkiah the priest [the] book of [the] law of Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And when they were bringing out the money that had been brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Moses.
en.B: As they were taking out the money brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priest Hilkiah found the book of the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, given through Moses.
en.R: While they were bringing out the money that had been brought to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Hilkiah the priest found the book of {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} teaching that was given through Moses.

decisions.choice: the book of the law of Yahweh: the book of Yahweh's instruction
decisions.reason: The word for "law" (torah) means instruction or teaching, the whole of what Yahweh taught through Moses, not only rules (Deuteronomy 1:5; 31:9). 2 Kings 22:8 calls it "the book of the law"; Chronicles names it more fully as Yahweh's and given through Moses. On which book this was, see the note at 2 Kings 22:8: what it leads Josiah to do matches Deuteronomy closely.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: given through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" a person means through him, as an agent. The law came from Yahweh and was given through Moses (35:6; Leviticus 8:36).

decisions.choice: found while the money was being brought out
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:8 does not say when the book was found; Chronicles ties the finding to the bringing out of the money for the repairs (verse 9). Kings gives Hilkiah's own words first; Chronicles tells the finding, then gives his words in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the book of the LORD's teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for torah, as at 2 Kings 22:8, because "law" alone makes most readers think only of rules (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "the book of the law".

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַן חִלְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־שָׁפָ֣ן הַסּוֹפֵ֔ר סֵ֧פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֛ה מָצָ֖אתִי בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֧ן חִלְקִיָּ֛הוּ אֶת־הַסֵּ֖פֶר אֶל־שָׁפָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Hilkiah and said to Shaphan the scribe, [the] book of the law I have found in [the] house of Yahweh; and gave Hilkiah the book to Shaphan.

en.L: And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, "The book of the law I have found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
en.B: Hilkiah spoke up and said to Shaphan the secretary, "In the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I have found the book of the law." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
en.R: Hilkiah told Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} teaching in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." He gave the book to Shaphan.

decisions.choice: Hilkiah's words: as in 2 Kings 22:8
decisions.reason: Hilkiah's words are the same as in 2 Kings 22:8. Chronicles says that he "answered and said", calls him only "Hilkiah" here, and does not say that Shaphan read the book before taking it to the king, as Kings does.

decisions.choice: answered and said: spoke up
decisions.reason: "Answered" often begins a speech that responds to a situation rather than to a question (1 Chronicles 12:18). Hilkiah speaks because of what he has found.

decisions.choice: Shaphan the scribe: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: The scribe was one of the king's chief officials, who kept records and handled royal business (2 Kings 22:3).

decisions.choice: the scribe / the secretary; the book of the law / the book of the LORD's teaching
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:8 where the Hebrew is the same. Balanced says "spoke up" for "answered" (m2), and Readable gives only "told".

source.text: וַיָּבֵ֨א שָׁפָ֤ן אֶת־הַסֵּ֨פֶר֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֨שֶׁב ע֧וֹד אֶת־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־נִתַּ֥ן בְּיַד־עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought Shaphan the book to the king, and he brought back further [to] the king word, saying, all that was given in [the] hand of your servants they [are] doing.

en.L: And Shaphan brought the book to the king, and further brought back word to the king, saying, "All that was given into the hand of your servants they are doing.
en.B: Shaphan took the book to the king and also reported to him: "Your officials are doing everything that was entrusted to them.
en.R: Shaphan took the book to the king and also gave him a report. "Your officials are doing everything you told them to do.

decisions.choice: brought back word to the king: reported to him
decisions.reason: To bring back a word is to give a report on a task one was sent to do, as in 2 Kings 22:9. "Further" adds the report to the bringing of the book.

decisions.choice: your servants: the king's officials
decisions.reason: Shaphan speaks of the men who carried out the king's order as the king's servants, his officials, as in 2 Kings 22:9.

decisions.choice: Shaphan brings the book with his report
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 22:9 Shaphan first reports on the money and only then speaks of the book (2 Kings 22:10). Here he brings the book to the king at the outset, and his report on the work runs into verse 17.

decisions.choice: your officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as throughout these books; Literal keeps "servants". Shaphan's report opens with a double quote mark here and closes at the end of verse 17.

source.text: וַיַּתִּ֕יכוּ אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַנִּמְצָ֣א בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּהוּ עַל־יַד֙ הַמֻּפְקָדִ֔ים וְעַל־יַ֖ד עוֹשֵׂ֥י הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they have poured out the money found in [the] house of Yahweh, and they have given it on [the] hand of those appointed and on [the] hand of [the] doers of the work.

en.L: And they have poured out the money that was found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and have given it into the hand of those who are appointed and into the hand of the doers of the work."
en.B: They have emptied out the money found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and handed it over to the overseers and to the men doing the work."
en.R: They have emptied out the money that was found in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They have given it to the men in charge and to the workers."

decisions.choice: poured out the money: emptied the chest
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 22:9, the verb means to pour out, most likely emptying the money out of the chest (24:8-11) to be counted and paid out. The same verb is used of melting metal (Ezekiel 22:20-22), so it may mean that the silver was melted down.

decisions.choice: the report as in 2 Kings 22:9
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Kings 22:9, which says "in the house" and gives the money to "the doers of the work, those appointed in the house of Yahweh". Chronicles says "in the house of Yahweh" and names the overseers and the workmen separately, as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: poured out / emptied out; those who are appointed / the overseers / the men in charge
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:9 where the Hebrew is the same. Shaphan's report closes here.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֞ד שָׁפָ֤ן הַסּוֹפֵר֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר סֵ֚פֶר נָ֣תַן לִ֔י חִלְקִיָּ֖הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַיִּקְרָא־ב֥וֹ שָׁפָ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And told Shaphan the scribe to the king, saying, [a] book has given to me Hilkiah the priest; and read in it Shaphan before the king.

en.L: And Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, "A book Hilkiah the priest has given me." And Shaphan read from it before the king.
en.B: Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has handed me a book." And Shaphan read from it aloud to the king.
en.R: Shaphan the secretary also told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then he read from it aloud to the king.

decisions.choice: a book: Shaphan names it without saying what it is
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 22:10, "a book" stands first in Shaphan's words, and he does not repeat Hilkiah's words "the book of the law" (verse 15).

decisions.choice: read in it before the king: read from it aloud
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:10 says that Shaphan "read it"; Chronicles says he "read in it", which may mean that he read parts of it. To read "before" someone is to read in his hearing (Deuteronomy 31:11).

decisions.choice: read from it; aloud
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:10, with "from it" for the Hebrew "in it" (m2). Balanced and Readable say "aloud" for what reading "before the king" means.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when heard the king the words of the law, and he tore his clothes.

en.L: And it was, when the king heard the words of the law, that he tore his clothes.
en.B: When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
en.R: When the king heard the words of {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} teaching, he tore his clothes in grief.

decisions.choice: he tore his clothes: a sign of grief and alarm
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the outward sign of grief, dismay or repentance (2 Kings 18:37; 19:1). The king sees that the words of the law stand against his people (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the words of the law: 2 Kings 22:11 says "the words of the book of the law"
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 22:11 except that Chronicles says "the words of the law". The sense is the same: what the book taught and warned.

decisions.choice: the LORD's teaching; in grief (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the law and adds whose it is, as in verse 14. It adds "in grief" to say what tearing the clothes meant (m1), as at 2 Kings 22:11.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־חִלְקִיָּ֡הוּ וְאֶת־אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־שָׁ֠פָן וְאֶת־עַבְדּ֨וֹן בֶּן־מִיכָ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת׀שָׁפָ֣ן הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וְאֵ֛ת עֲשָׂיָ֥ה עֶֽבֶד־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Hilkiah and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Abdon son of Micah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah [the] servant of the king, saying,

en.L: And the king commanded Hilkiah and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Abdon son of Micah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,
en.B: Then the king gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's official,
en.R: Then the king gave an order to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah, an official of the king. He said,

decisions.choice: Abdon son of Micah: called Achbor son of Micaiah in 2 Kings 22:12
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:12 names this man Achbor son of Micaiah. Micah is a short form of Micaiah; the two forms of the first name may come from different ways of writing it down. Chronicles also calls Hilkiah only by name, without "the priest".

decisions.choice: Ahikam son of Shaphan
decisions.reason: Ahikam was the son of Shaphan the secretary. He later protected the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:24), and his son Gedaliah was made governor of Judah after the fall of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:22).

decisions.choice: Asaiah the servant of the king: a title for a royal official
decisions.reason: "Servant of the king" was the title of a high officer serving the king directly, not a household slave, as at 2 Kings 22:12.

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 21
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the king's command, given in verse 21.

decisions.choice: the king's official (Balanced); an official of the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:12, with the names this verse gives.

source.text: לְכוּ֩ דִרְשׁ֨וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֜ה בַּעֲדִ֗י וּבְעַד֙ הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וּבִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַסֵּ֖פֶר אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצָ֑א כִּֽי־גְדוֹלָ֤ה חֲמַת־יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִתְּכָ֣ה בָ֔נוּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־שָׁמְר֤וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֖וּב עַל־הַסֵּ֥פֶר הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Go, inquire of Yahweh for me and for the [one] left in Israel and in Judah concerning [the] words of the book which has been found; for great [is] [the] wrath of Yahweh which has been poured out on us, because that not kept our fathers [the] word of Yahweh, to do according to all the written in the book the this.

en.L: "Go, inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for me and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found; for great [is] the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that has been poured out on us, because our fathers did not keep the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to do according to all that is written in this book."
en.B: "Go and ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on my behalf, and on behalf of those who are left in Israel and in Judah, about the words of the book that has been found. Great is {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} anger that has been poured out on us, because our ancestors did not keep the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or do all that is written in this book."
en.R: "Go and ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the words of this book that has been found. Ask for me and for the people who are left in Israel and in Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is very angry with us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger on us. This is because our ancestors did not obey the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They did not do what is written in this book."

decisions.choice: inquire of Yahweh: seek a word from Yahweh through a prophet
decisions.reason: To "seek" Yahweh in this sense is to ask for his answer on a matter, usually through a prophet (18:4-7; 2 Kings 22:13). The officials go to Huldah (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the king's command as in 2 Kings 22:13, with three differences
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:13 has "for the people and for all Judah"; Chronicles has "for those left in Israel and in Judah", taking in the survivors of the north (verse 9). Kings says that the wrath "has been kindled"; Chronicles that it "has been poured out". Kings says the fathers did not listen "to the words of this book"; Chronicles that they did not keep "the word of Yahweh".

decisions.choice: great is the wrath of Yahweh that has been poured out: his anger already falls on them
decisions.reason: The noun is a strong word for burning anger. Here it is pictured as poured out like a liquid (12:7), and the past tense shows that the king sees it as already falling on the land, in the losses of the years before (29:8-9).

decisions.choice: to do according to all that is written: what the book requires
decisions.reason: The fathers failed to keep Yahweh's word by not doing what the book laid down. Its curses now stand against the people (verse 24).

decisions.choice: inquire of / ask; wrath / anger; our fathers / our ancestors
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:13 where the Hebrew is the same, with "poured out" for the Chronicles verb at every level. Readable keeps the two sentences of 2 Kings 22:13 for the people for whom they ask, and says "obey" for "keep".

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶל־חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה אֵ֣שֶׁת׀שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן־תָּקְהַ֗ת בֶּן־חַסְרָה֙ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַבְּגָדִ֔ים וְהִ֛יא יוֹשֶׁ֥בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יהָ כָּזֹֽאת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And went Hilkiah and [those] whom the king [sent] to Huldah the prophetess, [the] wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments; and she [was] living in Jerusalem in the Second [Quarter]; and they spoke to her like this.

en.L: And Hilkiah and [those] whom the king [had sent] went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments; and she [was] living in Jerusalem in the Second [Quarter]; and they spoke to her to this [effect].
en.B: So Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to the prophet Huldah, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. Her home was in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem, and they spoke with her about this.
en.R: So Hilkiah and the men the king had sent went to Huldah. She was a prophet. Her husband was Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, the man in charge of the wardrobe. She lived in the newer part of Jerusalem called the Second Quarter. They told her what had happened.

decisions.choice: Hilkiah and those whom the king: a verb is missing
alternatives: Hilkiah and those whom the king had commanded
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Hilkiah and those whom the king", with no verb. The sense is clear from verse 20: the men the king had sent. The ancient Greek and Latin translations supply a verb such as "had commanded" or "had sent", and the words may have dropped out in copying.

decisions.choice: Huldah the prophetess: a woman who spoke Yahweh's word
decisions.reason: The noun is the feminine form of the word for "prophet", used also of Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Deborah (Judges 4:4). The king's officials, the high priest among them, go to her for Yahweh's answer.

decisions.choice: Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah: named a little differently in Kings
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:14 names Huldah's husband Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas. The names are close in form and most likely spellings of the same names. The letters written here read "Tokehath"; the margin reads "Tokhath", followed here.

decisions.choice: the Second Quarter: a newer district of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 22:14, the word means "second" and most likely names a part of the city added later, outside the oldest walls (Zephaniah 1:11). Where exactly it lay is not certain.

decisions.choice: they spoke to her like this: told her the matter
decisions.reason: "Like this" refers to what has gone before: they told her about the book and the king's question.

decisions.choice: the prophet; wardrobe; the newer part of Jerusalem called the Second Quarter
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:14: English now uses "prophet" for women and men alike, Literal keeps "prophetess". Literal brackets the missing verb (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And she said to them, thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, say to the man who sent you to me,

en.L: And she said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
en.B: She said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the man who sent you to me,
en.R: She told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Give this message to the man who sent you to me,

decisions.choice: thus says Yahweh: the messenger's formula
decisions.reason: A messenger began by naming the one whose words he carried. Prophets use the formula to show that what follows is Yahweh's word, not their own.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 22:15
decisions.reason: Huldah's opening is word for word the same as in 2 Kings 22:15. Before Yahweh's sentence on Judah, the king is "the man who sent you"; when the word turns to Josiah himself, she calls him "the king of Judah" (verse 26).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:15 at each level. Huldah's answer opens with a double quote mark here and closes at the end of her last words in verse 28; the messages within it open with single quote marks in verses 24 and 26.

source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה עַל־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְעַל־יוֹשְׁבָ֑יו אֵ֤ת כָּל־הָאָלוֹת֙ הַכְּתוּב֣וֹת עַל־הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָֽרְא֔וּ לִפְנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, here I [am] bringing evil on the place the this and on its inhabitants, all the curses the written on the book which they read before [the] king of Judah;

en.L: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] bringing evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the book that they read before the king of Judah,
en.B: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to bring disaster on this place and on those who live in it, all the curses written in the book that was read before the king of Judah,
en.R: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and on the people who live here. All the curses written in the book that was read to the king of Judah will happen.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm brought as punishment
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means evil done or evil suffered. Here it is the disaster Yahweh brings as judgment, not wrongdoing, as at 2 Kings 22:16.

decisions.choice: all the curses written in the book: 2 Kings 22:16 says "all the words of the book"
decisions.reason: Where 2 Kings 22:16 has "all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read", Chronicles names them as "all the curses" and says that "they read" it before the king (verse 18). The curses are those of the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:15-68; 29:19-27).

decisions.choice: look, I am bringing: about to happen
decisions.reason: The word "look" with the participle announces something that is sure and near.

decisions.choice: evil (Literal); disaster (Balanced, Readable); the curses
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:16 where the Hebrew is the same. Balanced and Readable say "was read" for the unnamed "they" who read the book. Readable makes the curses a sentence of their own and supplies "will happen", as at 2 Kings 22:16.

source.text: תַּ֣חַת׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּנִי וַֽיְקַטְּרוּ֙לֵֽאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְמַ֨עַן֙ הַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי בְּכֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יְדֵיהֶ֑ם וְתִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: because that they have forsaken me and they have burned incense to gods other, so as to provoke me to anger with all [the] works of their hands; and will be poured out my wrath on the place the this, and not it will be quenched.

en.L: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and have burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with all the works of their hands; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will be poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched.'
en.B: because they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and burned incense to other gods, provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with all the works of their hands. So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will pour out on this place, and it will not be put out.'
en.R: This will happen because they have left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and burned incense to other gods. They have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with all the idols they have made with their hands. So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will pour out on this place like fire, and no one will be able to put it out.'

decisions.choice: burned incense: or made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, of incense or of offerings burned on an altar. The letters written in the text and the reading in the margin give two forms of this verb with the same sense.

decisions.choice: provoke me to anger with the works of their hands: the words of Deuteronomy
alternatives: by all that they have done
decisions.reason: Moses warned that Israel would do evil and provoke Yahweh "with the work of your hands" (Deuteronomy 31:29). The works of their hands are the idols they made, and may take in all their deeds.

decisions.choice: my wrath will be poured out ... will not be quenched: 2 Kings 22:17 says "kindled"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 22:17, but where Kings says that Yahweh's wrath "will be kindled", Chronicles says it "will be poured out", as the king had said (verse 21). "Will not be quenched" still pictures it as fire: a sentence that will not be withdrawn (Jeremiah 7:20).

decisions.choice: forsaken / abandoned / left; poured out / pour out
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:17 where the Hebrew is the same, with "poured out" for the Chronicles verb. Readable keeps "like fire" so that the picture in "will not be quenched" is plain, as at 2 Kings 22:17. The single quote mark opened in verse 24 closes here.

source.text: וְאֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְכֶם֙ לִדְר֣וֹשׁ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלָ֑יוסכֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] king of Judah who sent you to inquire of Yahweh, thus you shall say to him, thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, the words which you have heard,

en.L: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: [As for] the words that you have heard,
en.B: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, say this: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: As for the words you have heard,
en.R: But say this to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the book: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says about the words you have heard:

decisions.choice: the words that you have heard: the sentence breaks off
decisions.reason: The phrase stands alone and is not finished; the sentence starts again in verse 27 with "because". It means "as for the words you have heard", the words of the book.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 22:18
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 22:18 except for a small change in how the verb "inquire" takes its object; the sense is the same. Huldah now names Josiah as king, where in verse 23 he was "the man who sent you".

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:18 at each level. A single quote mark opens the message for the king.

source.text: יַ֠עַן רַךְ־לְבָ֨בְךָ֜ וַתִּכָּנַ֣ע׀מִלִּפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֗ים בְּשָׁמְעֲךָ֤ אֶת־דְּבָרָיו֙ עַל־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ וְעַל־יֹ֣שְׁבָ֔יו וַתִּכָּנַ֣ע לְפָנַ֔י וַתִּקְרַ֥ע אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֖יךָ וַתֵּ֣בְךְּ לְפָנָ֑י וְגַם־אֲנִ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: because was soft your heart and you humbled yourself from before God when you heard his words against the place the this and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before me and you tore your clothes and you wept before me, and also I have heard, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before God when you heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and tore your clothes and wept before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I also have heard, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: because your heart was tender, and when you heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words against this place and its people you humbled yourself before God; and because you humbled yourself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, tore your clothes and wept before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I in turn have heard you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: When you heard what God said against this place and the people who live here, your heart was moved and you made yourself humble before God. You humbled yourself before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You tore your clothes and wept in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence. So I have listened to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your heart was soft: you were open and responsive, not hardened
decisions.reason: A soft heart takes a warning to heart and is moved by it; a hard heart refuses (36:13; Deuteronomy 2:30).

decisions.choice: Huldah's words as in 2 Kings 22:19, with differences
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 22:19 has "before Yahweh" and "what I spoke against this place", and adds that it would become "a desolation and a curse". Chronicles says "before God" and "his words", leaves out the desolation and the curse, and says a second time that Josiah humbled himself, now "before me": Yahweh himself speaks of the king's repentance.

decisions.choice: I also have heard: Yahweh has heard the king
decisions.reason: "I" is emphatic: as Josiah heard Yahweh's words, Yahweh in turn has heard him. "Declares Yahweh" seals the promise. Humbling oneself is a key word in Chronicles for the repentance Yahweh answers (7:14; 12:6-7; 33:12-13).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable); your heart was moved
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:19 where the Hebrew is the same. Readable gives the sense of the idiom (m1) and splits the long sentence into short ones.

source.text: הִנְנִ֨י אֹֽסִפְךָ֜ אֶל־אֲבֹתֶ֗יךָ וְנֶאֱסַפְתָּ֣ אֶל־קִבְרֹתֶיךָ֮ בְּשָׁלוֹם֒ וְלֹא־תִרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹל֙ הָֽרָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֥י מֵבִ֛יא עַל־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְעַל־יֹשְׁבָ֑יו וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Here I [am] gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your graves in peace, and not will look your eyes on all the evil which I [am] bringing on the place the this and on its inhabitants. And they brought back [to] the king word.

en.L: Look, I [am] gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your graves in peace, and your eyes will not look on all the evil that I [am] bringing on this place and on its inhabitants.'" And they brought back word to the king.
en.B: I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. You will not see with your own eyes all the disaster I am going to bring on this place and on those who live in it.'" Then they took her answer back to the king.
en.R: I will let you die and join your ancestors. You will be buried in peace, and you will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place and on the people who live here.'" Then the men took her answer back to the king.

decisions.choice: gather you to your fathers ... gathered to your graves: you will die and be buried with your ancestors
decisions.reason: To be gathered to one's fathers is to die and join those who have died before (Judges 2:10). "Graves" is plural, most likely the family tomb of the kings.

decisions.choice: in peace: before the disaster, and buried in his own tomb
alternatives: a promise of a peaceful death, which Josiah forfeited
decisions.reason: Josiah was killed in battle by Pharaoh Neco (35:20-24), so "in peace" does not mean a peaceful death. The verse explains it: his eyes would not see the disaster Yahweh would bring on Jerusalem. He died while Judah still stood and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors (35:24). Some read the promise as one Josiah lost by going out against Neco against God's warning (35:21-22).

decisions.choice: as in 2 Kings 22:20, without "therefore" and with "its inhabitants"
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Kings 22:20, which begins with "therefore" and speaks only of "this place". Chronicles adds "and on its inhabitants", as in verses 24 and 27.

decisions.choice: gathered to your grave (Balanced); buried (Readable); took her answer back
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 22:20 where the Hebrew is the same. Huldah's answer closes here, with both quote marks.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֕ף אֶת־כָּל־זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king and he gathered all [the] elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: And the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: Then the king sent word and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: Then King Josiah sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem and brought them together.

decisions.choice: the elders: the heads of families and towns
decisions.reason: The elders were the senior men who led the clans and towns and spoke for the people (2 Kings 23:1). The king calls them before he calls the whole nation (verse 30).

decisions.choice: he gathered: 2 Kings 23:1 says "they gathered to him"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 23:1, where the elders "gathered to him". Chronicles makes the king the one who gathered them.

decisions.choice: sent / sent word / sent for; gathered
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 23:1 where the Hebrew is the same. Readable names the king, as there.

records.literal_gloss: And went up the king [to the] house of Yahweh, and every man of Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from great and to small; and he read in their ears all [the] words of [the] book of the covenant found [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And the king went up [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and every man of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from great to small; and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found [in the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The king went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with him went {{gender:all the people of Judah|all the men of Judah}} and those who lived in Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least. In their hearing he read out all the words of the book of the covenant, which had been found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The king went up to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{gender:All the people of Judah|All the men of Judah}} and the people who lived in Jerusalem went with him. The priests and the Levites went too, and all the people, from the most important to the least important. The king read aloud to them everything written in the book of the covenant that had been found in {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} temple.

decisions.choice: the book of the covenant: the scroll found in the temple
decisions.reason: This is the book Hilkiah found, called "the book of the law of Yahweh" in verse 14. It is named here for what it contains: the terms of Yahweh's covenant with Israel (2 Kings 23:2).

decisions.choice: the Levites: 2 Kings 23:2 has "the prophets"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 23:2, with two differences: where Kings names "the priests and the prophets", Chronicles names "the priests and the Levites"; and Kings says "from small to great", Chronicles "from great to small". Chronicles gives the Levites a large place throughout Josiah's reform (verses 9, 12-13; 35:3).

decisions.choice: reading the covenant to the people: as Moses did at Sinai
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses read the book of the covenant in the hearing of the people, and they promised to obey (Exodus 24:7). Deuteronomy 31:10-13 commands the law to be read before all Israel.

decisions.choice: every man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: "Man of Judah" is used for the people of Judah taken together, as at 2 Kings 23:2.

decisions.choice: all the people of Judah
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:2, the phrase means the people of Judah as a whole (m4), so Balanced and Readable use the inclusive wording, with the traditional form as the alternative. The rest of the verse keeps the wording of 2 Kings 23:2, with "from the greatest to the least" for the reversed order.

records.literal_gloss: And stood the king at his place and cut the covenant before Yahweh, to walk after Yahweh and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to do [the] words of the covenant the written on the book the this.

en.L: And the king stood in his place and made the covenant before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to walk after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to do the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
en.B: The king stood in his place and made the covenant in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: to follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes with all his heart and all his being, and so to carry out the words of the covenant written in this book.
en.R: The king stood in his place and made a covenant in {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} presence. He promised to follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws with all his heart and all his life. He promised to do everything the covenant said, as it was written in this book.

decisions.choice: in his place: the king's standing place in the temple court
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:3 says "by the pillar", where the king had a set place at the temple (2 Kings 11:14; 2 Chronicles 23:13). Chronicles calls it his place.

decisions.choice: made the covenant before Yahweh: Israel's covenant renewed
decisions.reason: "The covenant" is the bond already known between Yahweh and his people. Making it "before Yahweh" means in his presence, with him as the one to whom the promise is made (2 Kings 23:3).

decisions.choice: commandments, testimonies and statutes: the whole of the covenant law
decisions.reason: The three words together name all that Yahweh requires (Deuteronomy 6:17), as at 2 Kings 23:3.

decisions.choice: with all his heart and with all his soul: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy asks Israel to love and serve Yahweh "with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deuteronomy 6:5; 10:12). Chronicles says "his heart" and "his soul" where 2 Kings 23:3 has "all the heart", and "to do the words" where Kings has "to establish the words"; the sense is the same. Kings goes on to say that all the people stood in the covenant; Chronicles tells their part in verse 32.

decisions.choice: commandments, testimonies, statutes / commandments, decrees, statutes / commands, instructions, laws
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 23:3 where the Hebrew is the same. Readable says plainly that making a covenant meant making a promise, as there.

records.literal_gloss: And he made stand all the [ones] found in Jerusalem and Benjamin; and did [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem according to [the] covenant of God, [the] God of their fathers.

en.L: And he made all who were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand [to it]; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.
en.B: He had everyone who was present in Jerusalem and Benjamin commit themselves to it, and the people of Jerusalem acted in keeping with the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.
en.R: Then he had all the people in Jerusalem and Benjamin promise to keep it. And the people of Jerusalem did what the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors, required.

decisions.choice: he made them stand: he had them take their stand on the covenant
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:3 says that "all the people stood in the covenant". Here the king "made" them stand, that is, had them commit themselves to it.

decisions.choice: and Benjamin: perhaps "in the covenant"
alternatives: he made all who were present in Jerusalem stand in the covenant
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "in Jerusalem and Benjamin". A very similar set of letters would read "in the covenant", giving "he made all present in Jerusalem stand in the covenant", as in 2 Kings 23:3. The Hebrew as it stands makes sense, since Benjamin's land lay next to Jerusalem, and it is followed.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant: they kept it
decisions.reason: To do "according to" the covenant is to live by its terms. The covenant is God's, and he is the God their ancestors had known.

decisions.choice: commit themselves to it (Balanced); promise to keep it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "made ... stand" (m1), as 2 Kings 23:3 does for "stood in the covenant". Literal brackets "to it".

records.literal_gloss: And removed Josiah all the abominations from all the lands which [belonged] to [the] sons of Israel, and he made serve all the [ones] found in Israel, to serve Yahweh their God; all his days not they turned aside from after Yahweh [the] God of their fathers.

en.L: And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the lands that belonged to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and made all who were present in Israel serve, to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. All his days they did not turn aside from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers.
en.B: Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands that belonged to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and he made everyone present in Israel serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. As long as he lived, they did not turn away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.
en.R: Josiah got rid of all the disgusting idols in all the land that belonged to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He made everyone in Israel worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. As long as Josiah lived, the people did not stop following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: the abominations: the idols and practices Yahweh detests
decisions.reason: The word names what is detestable to Yahweh, here the idols and objects of false worship (33:2; Deuteronomy 7:25-26).

decisions.choice: a summary of the reform told at length in 2 Kings 23:4-20, 24
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 23:4-20 and 24 tell in detail how Josiah cleared the temple, Jerusalem, Judah, Bethel and the towns of Samaria. Chronicles has told the purge already (verses 3-7) and here sums it up in one sentence after the covenant.

decisions.choice: made them serve, to serve Yahweh: he led them into Yahweh's worship
decisions.reason: The verb "serve" is used twice: Josiah made them serve, that is, to serve Yahweh. To serve a god is to worship him. Chronicles uses the same verb for Manasseh, who led Judah astray, and then commanded Judah to serve Yahweh (33:9, 16).

decisions.choice: all his days they did not turn aside: as long as Josiah lived
decisions.reason: The faithfulness of the people is tied to Josiah's lifetime. After his death his sons did evil (36:5, 9, 12), and the disaster Huldah had spoken of came (36:15-21).

decisions.choice: abominations / detestable things / disgusting idols
decisions.reason: The wording used for this word at 2 Kings 21:2 at each level, with "idols" at Readable because the things removed are objects (m1). Balanced and Readable say "as long as he lived" for "all his days".
